## 3. Detailed Summaries of the Two Top Preprints (150 words each)

### Preprint 1: GUIDE-seq 2.0 — Enhanced Genome-wide Off-target Profiling

GUIDE-seq 2.0 builds upon the original GUIDE-seq genome-wide off-target detection technology by improving integration efficiency of double-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide (dsODN) tags at DNA double-strand break sites created by Cas nucleases. Optimization includes modified tag chemistry and improved library preparation protocols that notably enhance sensitivity and specificity, allowing detection of rare off-target events previously missed. The method incorporates improved computational pipelines to filter background and accurately quantify off-target frequencies. Tested on clinically relevant human cell lines with commonly used sgRNA-Cas9 constructs, GUIDE-seq 2.0 detected off-target sites at lower editing rates (~0.01%), enabling comprehensive off-target landscape analysis. This method is non-disruptive to cell viability and compatible with a range of Cas variants, serving as a robust standard for future off-target analyses.

---

### Preprint 2: Rational Design of Ultra-high Fidelity Cas9 Variants (eCas9-X, HF-Cas9-Plus)

This preprint details the engineering of novel Cas9 variants through targeted amino acid substitutions designed to diminish non-specific DNA interactions and enhance kinetic proofreading during target recognition. Variants eCas9-X and HF-Cas9-Plus show substantially reduced tolerance for mismatches between the guide RNA and DNA, thereby lowering off-target cleavage rates by over 90% compared to wild-type Cas9, as assessed with GUIDE-seq and CIRCLE-seq methods. Importantly, on-target editing efficiency remains comparable to wild-type levels. The study employs biophysical assays and live-cell imaging to correlate reduced DNA binding dwell time with increased specificity. These ultra-high-fidelity nucleases represent a promising advance towards safer therapeutic applications of CRISPR gene editing.
